physics: The public series spring/dashpot mechanics gives tau*T_dot+T=kappa*v. With the stated exp(-i*omega*t) convention the scaled impedance is alpha/(1-i*omega*tau), has positive real part, and the front/rear traction signs oppose fluid slip.

The modal polynomial and independent BVP both implement E_zz+omega^2*E=-i*omega*J and nu*J_zz=(gamma-i*omega)*J-p^2*E. Front incoming and rear outgoing Maxwell boundary signs agree; no viscous mode or known control is omitted.

For scaled traction a=q*T/m and J=q*n0*v, a*J/p^2 is mechanical power, whereas a^2/(alpha*p^2) is dashpot heat. Real-field multiplication and normalization by E0^2/2 give q0=abs(a)^2/(alpha*p^2), q2=a^2/(alpha*p^2), and source w2=a*J/p^2. The documented sine readout is Im(q2), with no sign or factor2 discrepancy.

Mean work equals mean heat at every p/control because the spring returns to its initial energy after one period. At finite memory w2=(1-i*omega*tau)*q2. Both controls therefore share the nonzero, finite-memory calibration while differing in the specified thermostat readout.

The reference obtains the fields from a real collocation BVP and integrates the actual contact ODE, periodic initial traction and squared dashpot power in time. It does not insert the oracle harmonic correction into the measured quantity. Shared continuum equations are appropriate and the independence is field/time numerical evaluation rather than microscopic material theory.

Normal incidence, fixed optical planes, a temperature-independent energetic spring, a fast dashpot-only thermostat and the incident-field phase fix the observable. Weak-field and steady-state limits are explicit. Bulk and rear heating are separate. Positive optical bulk/contact dissipation supports uniqueness of the driven passive field problem.
